title: Duty rosters, roll call, badges & attendance
summary: One duty roster for all staff with scoped planners (HR, Head Nurse, Ops), rest days rotating through a week that includes Sunday, the week check, duty swaps between colleagues, roll call where there is no badge station, attendance measured against the rostered shift, and badges that work with RFID, printed QR codes or biometrics.

# Duty rosters, roll call, badges & attendance

## Who rosters whom

One roster covers every kind of staff. The planner is the same screen in three workspaces; the server decides
whom each person may see and change, by the employee's staff category:

| Permission | Default role | May roster |
|---|---|---|
| `roster.manage.all` | HR Admin | every employee (doctors, lab, pharmacy, reception, nurses, support staff …) |
| `roster.manage.nursing` | Head Nurse | `Nursing` staff |
| `roster.manage.support` | Ops Admin | `SupportZeroInterface` staff (sweepers, janitors, guards) |
| `roster.view.all` | Owner, Hospital Admin (and HR) | read-only, everyone |

The Super Admin can move these permissions to other roles in the Role Access Matrix (for example a department
head). Everyone with a login sees their own duties (`GET /self/roster`).

## The planner (screens `duty_roster_hr`, `duty_roster`, `support_roster`)

1. `GET /rosters/staff?date_from=…&date_to=…` → the people you may roster (left column) with their approved
   `leave` in the range (grey those days out), the active `shift_patterns` (the grid's rows: Morning 08–14,
   Evening 14–20 and Night 20–08 are seeded; HR edits them at `POST /hr/shift-patterns`) and the public
   `holidays` in the range (mark those columns; rostering on them is allowed).
2. `GET /rosters?date_from=…&date_to=…[&ward_id|department_id|staff_category]` → the entries (a week by
   default, up to 62 days). Each has `row_version`, `shift_name`, `start_time`/`end_time` and `bed_ids`.
3. Drag people onto cells, then save everything at once: `POST /rosters {entries: [...]}`. It is all or
   nothing: on an error, `details.entry_index` names the entry to highlight.
   * `duty_area`: `Ward` (needs `ward_id`; the Head Nurse assigns `bed_ids` — the nurse then sees them in
     `GET /ipd/my-beds`), `Department`, `Emergency`, `OT`, `Facility` (gates, corridors, zones), `Other`.
   * `is_on_call`, `zone_label` and `notes` are free to use. The ER shows the duties in the `Emergency` area and every
     on-call duty of the moment (with the mobile number of whoever is on call) at `GET /er/on-duty` (MSDS 17 iii).
   * The ward of a duty from `GET /beds/matrix?include_beds=false`, the department of a `Department` duty from
     `GET /admin/departments` (decision 62); `PATCH /rosters/{id}` and `POST /rosters/copy` take them the same way.
4. Change one entry: `PATCH /rosters/{id}` with only the changed fields and `expected_version` (else
   `VERSION_CONFLICT` — reload). Remove one: `POST /rosters/{id}/cancel {reason}` (never deleted).
5. "Repeat last week": `POST /rosters/copy {source_from, source_to, target_from}` → `created` and `skipped`
   (with the reason per entry, e.g. `ROSTER_ON_LEAVE`). Show the skipped list.
6. Keep the grid live with the `roster.changed` event. Rostered staff who have a login also get a notification.

| Error | Meaning | UI |
|---|---|---|
| `ROSTER_OUT_OF_SCOPE` | that employee's staff category is not yours | should not happen if you only offer `/rosters/staff` |
| `ROSTER_CONFLICT` | overlaps another duty of the same person; a night shift runs into the next morning | highlight both cells |
| `ROSTER_ON_LEAVE` | approved leave that day | grey the day out |
| `ROSTER_DATE_CLOSED` | a past date, and you are not HR | past columns read-only |
| `ROSTER_EMPLOYEE_INACTIVE` | resigned / suspended / not yet submitted by HR | drop from the list |

A shift that crosses midnight belongs to the date it starts, for rostering and for attendance (below).
Back-to-back shifts (Night then Morning) are allowed; overlapping ones are not.

## The hospital never closes: rotating rest days

Sunday is a working day like any other, usually with fewer staff. Nobody is off just because it is Sunday: each
person gets their weekly rest day (setting `weekly_rest_days`, 1 by default, per **roster week**, which starts on
setting `roster_week_start_day`, Monday by default) on a different day, and the days rotate so that Sunday duty is
shared in turn.

* **Roster-only staff** (nurses, support staff): a day without a duty is a rest day. Plan the week, then use
  `POST /rosters/copy {source_from, source_to, target_from, "rotate_days": 1}` to repeat it with everyone's days
  moved on by one: a Monday-Saturday week with Sunday off becomes Tuesday-Sunday with Monday off, so over seven
  weeks everyone has each weekday off once. `rotate_days` 0 (the default) repeats the week as it was.
* **Staff on a fixed schedule** (accounts, office): their default shift names **their own** weekly days off
  (`weekly_off_days`, required: there is no hospital-wide day off). `GET /rosters/staff` shows them as
  `default_weekly_off_days`: grey those columns. Rostering them on that day makes it a working day.

### The week check (`GET /rosters/week`)

`GET /rosters/week?week_of=…[&ward_id|department_id|staff_category]` (any day of the week; today by default), for the
staff you may see:

* `staff[]`: each person's `duty_dates`, `rest_dates`, `leave_dates` and `working_days`, and `status`:
  `NoRestDay` (more working days than the week allows: `extra_duty_days` of them are paid as extra duty, see
  [HR and payroll](hr-and-payroll.md)), `NotRostered` (roster-only, nothing planned yet) or `Ok`.
  `staff_without_rest_day` counts the first.
* `days[]`: per day (`weekday` 7 = Sunday, `holiday_name`), how many are `on_duty`, `on_leave` and `resting`, and
  per shift (`shifts[].staff`). Show it as a row under the grid: a thin Sunday shows before the week starts.
* With `ward_id`: the staff with a duty on that ward that week, and only that ward's duties in the counts.

## Duty swaps between colleagues

A nurse with a personal emergency asks a colleague to work her duty (a **cover**), or to exchange duties (a
**swap**: she works one of the colleague's duties in return). Nothing changes on the roster until the colleague
agrees and a roster manager of their staff category approves (setting `roster_swap_needs_approval`; off = the
colleague's acceptance is enough). Self-service needs `self.roster.swap` (every role with a login and leave).

1. The requester, on a duty that has not started: `GET /self/roster/swap-options?roster_id=…` → `colleagues`: active
   staff of her category who are free then (no leave, no overlapping duty), same department first, each with
   `their_duties` of the next two weeks and `you_can_work_it`.
2. `POST /self/roster/swaps {roster_id, covering_employee_id, return_roster_id?, reason}` → status `Requested`; the
   colleague is notified. Refusals: `FORBIDDEN` (not your duty), `SWAP_DUTY_STARTED`, `SWAP_COLLEAGUE_INELIGIBLE`
   (`details.reason`: other_category, inactive, same_person), `ROSTER_CONFLICT` / `ROSTER_ON_LEAVE` (either of them
   cannot work the other's duty), `SWAP_EXISTS` (one open request per duty).
3. The colleague: `GET /self/roster/swaps` (`my_role` Colleague) → `POST /self/roster/swaps/{id}/accept {note?}` or
   `/decline {note?}`. The requester may `POST /self/roster/swaps/{id}/cancel` until it is approved.
4. The roster manager: `GET /rosters/swaps` (open ones; `Accepted` = waiting for you) →
   `POST /rosters/swaps/{id}/approve {note?}` or `/reject {note}`. Approval re-checks everything, then cancels each
   duty ("Worked by … (duty swap n)") and re-creates it for the other person with `swap_id`; both are notified.
   Neither colleague decides their own swap (`SWAP_SELF_APPROVAL`, also enforced by the database).
5. Staff without a login (sweepers, guards): the manager records the swap they agreed in person,
   `POST /rosters/swaps {roster_id, covering_employee_id, return_roster_id?, reason}`: accepted and approved at once.

A request still open when one of its duties starts expires (worker job `rosters.swap_expiry`); moving or cancelling
the duty on the roster withdraws it. Keep lists live with `roster.swap.updated`. Attendance follows the new duties.
A cover leaves the requester without a duty that day, a rest day; if the hospital wants it counted, she applies for
leave for it. The colleague's extra day may make theirs a seven-day week: paid as extra duty.

## Attendance is measured against the schedule (§6.4)

The worker computes each day's flag (`Present`, `Late`, `HalfDay`, `Absent`, `Leave`, `Off`) against the
employee's **schedule** for that day:

1. the day's duty roster entries (the earliest one sets the start time for lateness), also on a public holiday;
2. without an entry, the employee's **default shift** (`POST /hr/employees/{id}/shift`), for staff on a fixed
   schedule such as accounts, except on their own weekly days off (`weekly_off_days`) and public holidays;
3. with neither, the day is a paid rest day: `Holiday` on a public holiday, else `Off`.

Weekly days off and the holiday calendar (kept by HR and the Hospital Admin):
[HR, provisioning, attendance, leave & payroll](hr-and-payroll.md).

Staff planned week by week on the roster (nurses, support staff) should therefore have **no** default shift:
`POST /hr/employees/{id}/shift {"shift_pattern_id": null, "effective_from": "…"}` (the days before keep the old
default). Otherwise the default shift is expected on every day they are not rostered, and the rest day after a
night shift shows as `Absent`, which payroll deducts as an unpaid day. The planner shows each person's
`default_shift_pattern_id` (`GET /rosters/staff`) so the screen can warn about it.

### Night shifts

Every punch belongs to the **duty** it is for, not to its calendar date (`attendance_date` on each punch):

* The Night shift of the 5th (20:00–08:00) owns both the 19:55 arrival and the 08:05 exit on the 6th. The flag is
  on the 5th, with the worked time across midnight; the 6th stays a rest day.
* A punch counts for a scheduled duty from `attendance_early_punch_minutes` (default 180) before the duty starts
  to `attendance_late_punch_minutes` (default 360) after it ends. If it fits two duties (a night followed by a
  morning shift), it closes the earlier one while that is still open (an odd number of punches), else it opens
  the later one.
* A punch with no scheduled duty around it counts on its calendar date.
* `GET /hr/attendance/punches?employee_id=…&day=…` lists the punches of one duty date. When the automatic choice is
  wrong (forgotten punches in a double shift, unscheduled overtime), HR names the duty of a correction:
  `POST /hr/attendance/manual {…, "attendance_date": "…"}` (the punch's own date or the day before or after).
* A night shift that is still running after midnight stays on screen: the nurse's `GET /ipd/my-beds` and
  `GET /self/roster`, and the roll-call sheet.

Punches come from three sources, shown in `GET /hr/attendance/punches` (`source`):

| Source | How |
|---|---|
| `Badge` | a badge presented at a badge station (below) |
| `RollCall` | a supervisor marked the person present (below) |
| `Manual` | HR corrected a missed punch (`POST /hr/attendance/manual`, reason required) |

## Roll call — no badge station at all (screens `roll_call`, `support_roster`, HR `attendance`)

1. `GET /rosters/roll-call[?roster_date&shift_pattern_id&ward_id]` → who is rostered in your scope, with
   `first_in` / `first_source` for those already recorded. Without `roster_date`: today's duties plus a night
   shift from yesterday that is still running (each entry carries its own `roster_date`).
2. Tick who is present: `POST /rosters/roll-call {roster_date, present: [{employee_id, at?}]}` → an `In` punch
   for that duty, with source `RollCall` and you as the recorder; the duty's flag is recomputed at once. Staff who
   already punched for that duty are skipped (a badge scan is never doubled).
   * Open for today's duties and for a night shift that is still running (after midnight, send its
     `roster_date`: yesterday).
   * An earlier day's shift that has ended: HR only, with the real arrival time `at` (`ROSTER_DATE_CLOSED` for
     others).
   * `at` (default now) must fall within the shift, from 3 hours before it starts to 6 hours after it ends by
     default; a future `roster_date` is refused (`VALIDATION_ERROR`).

Requires `attendance.roll_call` (Head Nurse, Ops Admin, HR). Only rostered staff can be marked
(`ROLL_CALL_NOT_ROSTERED`).

## Badges and badge stations — zero-interface staff (§6.8, §8.2)

Sweepers, janitors and guards never log in and never use a keyboard. They present a **badge** at a **badge
station**. The hospital chooses the hardware; the API is identical:

| Hospital has | Badge (`technology`) | Station (`device_type`) |
|---|---|---|
| RFID readers | RFID card; HR enters the card UID as `badge_code` | `RFIDReader` (wall reader, ESP32, vendor gateway) |
| **No special hardware** | **`Barcode`: a QR printed on the staff ID card; the server generates the code** | **`BarcodeScanner`: any PC or tablet with a basic USB barcode scanner or its camera, running the kiosk page** |
| Fingerprint / face terminals | `Biometric`: the device's enrolment id | `BiometricTerminal` behind a small gateway that posts scans |

A hospital may mix them (one active badge per technology per person).

### Setting up without RFID

1. HR: `POST /hr/employees/{id}/badges {"technology": "Barcode", "holder_type": "Sweeper"}` → a code like
   `HB7K3M9Q2XW1` (unguessable). Print the ID card again: `GET /hr/employees/{id}/id-card` carries it as
   `badge` (`qr_svg`, `barcode_svg`). A lost card: `POST /hr/badges/{code}/revoke`, issue a new one, reprint.
2. IT: `PUT /admin/badge-stations/{id}` with `device_type: "BarcodeScanner"`, then
   `POST /admin/badge-stations/{id}/rotate-key` (the key is shown once; enter it in the kiosk's settings).
   * Staff entrance: `action_type: "AttendancePunch"`.
   * Bed cleaning: one kiosk per ward (`location_type: "Ward"`, `action_type: "BedCleaned"`, `ward_id`) and a QR
     sticker on every bed: print them from `GET /admin/wards/{ward_id}/bed-labels`. The cleaner scans the bed's
     sticker and their badge.
3. The kiosk page (screen `badge_station_kiosk`, workspace `badge_station`, no login):
   `GET /badge-stations/me?station_id=…` (header `X-Station-Key`) tells it what it does and whether it needs a
   bed sticker (`needs_bed_code`; `dirty_beds` lists what is waiting). Each scan:
   `POST /badge-stations/scans {station_id, badge_code, bed_code?, gateway_event_id}` → show `outcome` big and
   green / red: `AttendanceIn`, `AttendanceOut`, `BedCleaned`, `BedCleaningRecorded`, `SecurityPass`,
   `Duplicate`, `UnknownBadge`, `InactiveBadge`, `Rejected` (with `detail`), `NoAction`.

### Where there is no station at a bed or ward

The ward nurse, head nurse or ops admin confirms the cleaning on their screen:
`POST /beds/{bed_id}/mark-cleaned {"cleaned_by_employee_id": …}` (the cleaner is optional but attributes the
work; pick them with `GET /staff/lookup?q=`). Same rules as a scan: the bed becomes `Available`, or `BedCleaningRecorded` until discharge billing clears.

## Live facility feed (Ops)

Every scan, even a rejected one, is in `GET /ops/facility-feed` and the `ops.badge.scan` event.
